title: Streaming coalescer compact + stable KV lease protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our continuous request coalescer and the KV lease/heartbeat machinery have accumulated incremental fixes and special-cases over 18 months. This has increased tail latency variance under realistic mixed workloads and made rolling upgrades fragile (lease handoff races seen during small-scale canaries). Scope: Replace the ad-hoc coalescing paths with a compact streaming coalescer (a single, deterministic ingress path for small, medium, and streaming requests) and introduce a simplified, single-writer KV lease protocol with explicit handoff semantics and bounded backoff. Goals: 1) Reduce 99th percentile token latency variance by 20% on mixed chat workloads. 2) Eliminate observed lease handoff races under rolling deploys. 3) Reduce code complexity in the coalescer/ingress surface (target: -25% LOC in the subsystem). 4) Keep behavior backward compatible for dedicated/private clusters via a feature flag. Non-Goals: This ticket does not change model execution kernels or scheduling heuristics for GPU assignment. It also does not implement cross-region lease migration. Proposed approach: - Add a compact streaming coalescer component that normalizes request shapes and routes them into three stable lanes (interactive, bulk, streaming) with a shared admission-tracker. The coalescer will use sequence-aware batching hints rather than per-request special-cases. - Replace the current lease heartbeat mesh with a single-writer lease protocol: each shard maintains one authoritative lease-holder, explicit PREPARE/COMMIT/RELINQUISH transitions, and a bounded exponential backoff for contested handoffs. - Introduce a lease handoff test harness to reproduce timing windows seen in canaries (scripts live in infra/lease-tests). - Add telemetry: lease-transition histogram, coalescer-latency per-lane, and handoff-failure rate alerted at 0.5% of transitions. - Gate the new protocol behind runtime feature flag "compact_coalescer_v2" for safe rollout. Trade-offs and rationale: - The single-writer lease simplifies reasoning at the expense of sometimes higher latencies when a lease transfer is required; mitigated by batching handoffs and optimistic read-cache for hot keys. - Deterministic coalescer lanes reduce special-case logic but require careful admission tuning; we'll allow lane admission weights to be tuned via config. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and run e2e lease-handoff tests in CI. 2) Canary on small dedicated pool with telemetry enabled (48h). 3) Gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) controlled by rollback if handoff-failure > 0.5% or 99p latency regresses. 4) After 2 successful full canaries, remove old paths and flip the flag by default. Metrics and success criteria: - 99p token latency down 20% vs baseline on mixed chat. - Lease handoff failure rate < 0.1% in steady state. - No increase in tail error rates or OOM events. Testing: unit tests for protocol transitions, deterministic integration tests in lease-test-harness, and a synthetic latency validator that replays production traffic traces. Backout plan: immediate feature-flag flip to disable new coalescer and revert to current lease mesh. If unable to disable quickly, cluster-level traffic steering to older pool. Safety and security: no new secrets; default-off for private deployments until KMS audit. Docs: new design doc and runbook to be published to Confluence.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end CI passes including lease-handshake tests. 2) Canary telemetry meets success criteria for two consecutive canaries. 3) Code review approvals from runtime and infra owners. 4) Updated runbook and rollback steps in Confluence.

2026-02-20 - Design review with runtime team: agreed on single-writer lease and explicit RELINQUISH. Concern raised about handoff thundering; plan to add jittered backoff and optimistic reads.
2026-02-25 - Prototype landed (internal branch). Microbench shows coalescer lane normalization reduces per-request allocations by ~18%.
2026-02-28 - QA notes: integration test uncovered stale-cache window during handoff; fixed by adding 'handoff-ack' phase and re-run tests.
